title: Presidential Extra-Territorialization: How Presidents Go Abroad to Bypass Domestic Constraint
description: Introduces the concept of presidential extra-territorialization, whereby presidents use executive agreements to act through foreign jurisdictions and evade domestic legal or political constraints, engaging in jurisdictional arbitrage to accomplish policy goals affecting US citizens' rights that would be blocked domestically.

venue: In US Cultural Diplomacy after the Cold War (Manchester University Press)
title: The President as Cultural Diplomat: Donald Trump, the Presidency, and American Cultural Diplomacy
description: Analysis of how presidential conduct shapes American cultural diplomacy and soft power.

venue: In Transatlantic Storms and Transatlantic Relations (Georgetown University Press)
title: The First World War and the Anglo-American Crisis of 1916
description: Analyzes a little-studied international crisis which occurred between the United States and the United Kingdom in 1916 and which both sides feared may lead to war, showing that the Wilson administration's policy towards the war was more historically contingent than often realized.

title: Civilizational Wilsonianism from Woodrow Wilson to Donald Trump
description: Challenges the view that Trump's foreign policy broke with Wilsonianism, arguing that both Wilson and Trump's approaches were premised on ensuring the survival of a racially-defined Western civilization in a globalized world, revealing illiberal continuities in American foreign policy.

title: Competing and Complementary Regions in U.S. Foreign Policy
description: Argues that US foreign policy discussions overemphasize competition for resources between global regions and military power, while underemphasizing how complementarities between regions can advance American goals and the value of softer diplomatic tools.

title: Counterinsurgency Comes Home
description: Argues against applying counterinsurgency theory and civil war concepts to challenges facing American democracy, warning that such frameworks risk normalizing state violence, misdiagnosing political opposition as insurgency, and undermining democratic principles in the name of defending them.

title: Wat als Oekraïne na een vredesakkoord zélf de confrontatie zoekt?
description: Written shortly after the 'Coalition of the Willing' published a framework for peace in Ukraine, this article explores the stabilizing role the EU can play in stabilizing the Ukraine War and how it can best prepare itself for the threat of Russian aggression and Ukrainian revisionism.

title: The US Pivot to Asia Depends on Peace in Ukraine
description: Shortly before Trump assumed office, Martijn and Andrew published an article on the upcoming challenge for the new Trump administration regarding the necessity to stabilize the conflict in Europe and pivot its attention and resources to Asia. They set out how these US foreign policy objectives are connected and how the US can best balance its commitment to both.

venue: Heidelberg Spring Academy, University of Heidelberg, Heidelberg, Germany
title: VISTA and VESPRA in Puerto Rico
description: Presented about the role of VESPRA, a local volunteer community development program, and VISTA in Puerto Rico in the 1960s. Participant in the Heidelberg Spring Academy, a week-long conference for PhD students in American studies where they can receive intensive feedback about their projects from peers and experts in the field.

venue: British International History Group, University of East Anglia, Norwich, United Kingdom
title: Modernization and U.S. volunteer service programs
description: Presented an overview of her PhD research about the role of volunteer service programs in the liminal spaces of U.S. empire.

title: Trump's Cabinet dramatically changed American foreign policy while the president made noise – a scholar of presidential rhetoric explains
description: Examines how Trump's Cabinet members—Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth—have articulated the administration's foreign policy direction through carefully crafted rhetoric, while the president's chaotic communication style creates uncertainty. Argues that Cabinet statements offer clearer insight into actual policy than Trump's unpredictable social media posts, pointing to three major shifts: redefining Western values, prioritizing transactional relationships over humanitarian aid, and emphasizing military force over diplomatic solutions.

title: War in Ukraine: When the CIA Enters the Diplomatic Ballet
description: Analysis of the CIA's role in diplomatic efforts regarding the Ukraine conflict.

title: Trump's Press Exclusion Strategy
description: Discussion of how Trump uses press exclusion to set the tone in politics.

title: Falklands Tensions Rise Under Milei and Trump
description: Analysis of why the Falkland Islands remain a pressure point for the U.K. and how recent actions by Milei and Trump are stoking new tensions.

title: Canada Defends French Language Amid Trump Trade War
description: How Canada is defending linguistic sovereignty in the face of U.S. trade pressure.

title: Bessent Threatens New Iran Secondary Sanctions
description: Coverage of new secondary sanctions threats against Iran and international cooperation efforts.
